warrior: Mercenary: 'My left greave is cracked.' Warrior: 'Stuff straw inside it and keep your shield up.'
Mercenary: 'Think the crown will pay our back-wages?' Warrior: 'Only if we pry it off their fingers.'
Mercenary: 'That bridge looks narrow.' Warrior: 'Good. Means only three of them can swing at once.'
Mercenary: 'My knees ache when fog rolls in.' Warrior: 'Means you're still alive to complain.'
Mercenary: 'Why don't we charge?' Warrior: 'Because pikemen love men who run onto their points.'
Mercenary: 'How many sieges have you survived?' Warrior: 'Enough to know banners don't stop arrows.'
Mercenary: 'The rations smell like wet dog.' Warrior: 'Eat it anyway; starving men drop their shields.'
Mercenary: 'Do we bury their dead?' Warrior: 'Only if someone pays extra for shovel-work.'
Mercenary: 'What if the gate holds?' Warrior: 'Then we bring heavier wedges and hit the hinges.'
Mercenary: 'You never polish your breastplate.' Warrior: 'Bright steel makes an easy target at dusk.'
Mercenary: 'Should I guard the mage?' Warrior: 'Keep two paces ahead of his elbows or get singed.'
Mercenary: 'Think we'll see spring?' Warrior: 'Check your cinch-straps and we'll find out.'
Mercenary: 'My shield-arm aches.' Warrior: 'Better sore than severed. Keep it high.'
Mercenary: 'How many more miles?' Warrior: 'Until the mud turns to stone or we do.'
Mercenary: 'Their line looks thick.' Warrior: 'Good. Harder for them to run away.'
Mercenary: 'I'm out of whetstone.' Warrior: 'Use a river-pebble and stop complaining.'
Mercenary: 'My boots are full of bog-water.' Warrior: 'Walk faster and warm it up.'
Mercenary: 'What if they flank us?' Warrior: 'Then we turn around and break those too.'
Mercenary: 'That brute's huge.' Warrior: 'Means his knees are right at sword-height.'
Mercenary: 'Should we sound the horn?' Warrior: 'Save your breath for swinging.'
Mercenary: 'Think the tavern's still standing?' Warrior: 'If it isn't, we drink outside.'
Mercenary: 'My mail's rusting solid.' Warrior: 'Oil it tonight or wear it like a barrel.'
Mercenary: 'Arrows incoming!' Warrior: 'Lock rims and tuck your chin!'
Mercenary: 'They're chanting something.' Warrior: 'Shut their mouths with steel.'
Mercenary: 'I miss dry bread.' Warrior: 'Win this fight and you can buy a bakery.'
Mercenary: 'Fog's getting thick.' Warrior: 'Stay elbow-to-elbow and watch the ground.'
Mercenary: 'One of them dropped a gold ring.' Warrior: 'Leave it till the last one stops twitching.'
Mercenary: 'My helmet visor's bent.' Warrior: 'Rip it off; you don't need beauty today.'
Mercenary: 'Do we take prisoners?' Warrior: 'Only if they're carrying the pay-chest.'
Mercenary: 'That ash stings the eyes.' Warrior: 'Squint and swing at anything moving.'
Mercenary: 'We're outnumbered two to one.' Warrior: 'Fair odds for honest steel.'
Mercenary: 'Hold the gate!' Warrior: 'Plant your heels! Nothing passes this line!'
archer: Mercenary: 'Why do you keep checking the grass?' Archer: 'Wind shifts five degrees before the rain hits.'
Mercenary: 'My armor weighs forty pounds.' Archer: 'Sounds noisy. Try walking ten paces behind me.'
Mercenary: 'Did you see that shadow move?' Archer: 'Already put a bodkin through its shoulder.'
Mercenary: 'How many arrows do you carry?' Archer: 'Enough for them, plus two for anyone who touches my quiver.'
Mercenary: 'Should I rush their line?' Archer: 'Wait until I drop the one holding the big horn.'
Mercenary: 'You smiled when that bridge burned.' Archer: 'Saves us walking across an obvious ambush.'
Mercenary: 'Can you hit that crow on the spire?' Archer: 'Pay me a copper and I'll clip its tail-feathers.'
Mercenary: 'Why avoid the main road?' Archer: 'Wide roads are built for taxmen and cavalry.'
Mercenary: 'My shield has three arrows in it.' Archer: 'Better your oak than my ribs. Keep holding it.'
Mercenary: 'Do you ever miss?' Archer: 'Once, in sixty-four. Still irritates me.'
Mercenary: 'What's in that green vial?' Archer: 'Bog-viper bile. Don't lick your thumb after touching it.'
Mercenary: 'Are we lost?' Archer: 'No, just taking the scenic route around their crossbows.'
Mercenary: 'Wind's shifting east.' Archer: 'Aim two fingers left and let fly.'
Mercenary: 'Down to six bodkins.' Archer: 'Make six corpses and borrow theirs.'
Mercenary: 'My bowstring's damp.' Archer: 'Wax it now or snap it later.'
Mercenary: 'Can you hit that bannerman?' Archer: 'Already picked which eye.'
Mercenary: 'Reeds are moving ahead.' Archer: 'Nock broadheads; hounds hate iron.'
Mercenary: 'That ridge looks steep.' Archer: 'Climb it anyway—high ground wins fights.'
Mercenary: 'Too much smoke to see!' Archer: 'Shoot at the sparks from their armor.'
Mercenary: 'They're raising tower shields.' Archer: 'Wait for them to step, then take the ankles.'
Mercenary: 'My fingers are numb.' Archer: 'Blow on them and keep drawing.'
Mercenary: 'Heard a twig snap.' Archer: 'Keep walking; I've got the brush covered.'
Mercenary: 'Should I loose now?' Archer: 'Hold... let them clear the trees first.'
Mercenary: 'Nice shot through the visor!' Archer: 'Lucky wind. Keep moving.'
Mercenary: 'Midge-bites everywhere.' Archer: 'Scratch after we're out of range.'
Mercenary: 'Their shaman's in the back.' Archer: 'Not for long. Watch the red hood.'
Mercenary: 'Quiver's getting light.' Archer: 'Stop shooting at shields then.'
Mercenary: 'Why carry two strings?' Archer: 'Because one snaps when you're ten paces from death.'
Mercenary: 'Salt air ruins fletching.' Archer: 'Trim the feathers and quit whining.'
Mercenary: 'Footprints in the silt.' Archer: 'Fresh ones. Stay off the open path.'
Mercenary: 'They're charging!' Archer: 'Loose one more volley, then draw knives!'
Mercenary: 'Clean through the throat.' Archer: 'Saves us burying him.'
mage: Mercenary: 'My hair is standing straight up.' Mage: 'Step three paces left; you're standing on a ley-node.'
Mercenary: 'Can you light our campfire?' Mage: 'I am an arcana scholar, not a flint-and-steel.'
Mercenary: 'What was that purple flash?' Mage: 'An exothermic miscalculation. Nobody lost an eyebrow.'
Mercenary: 'Why carry so many notebooks?' Mage: 'Unrecorded anomalies are just expensive guesswork.'
Mercenary: 'Keep those sparks off my powder kegs!' Mage: 'Then stop parking your wagons inside my blast radius.'
Mercenary: 'Does magic hurt?' Mage: 'Only when a bandit interrupts the third consonant.'
Mercenary: 'Why smell like burnt copper?' Mage: 'Proper grounding prevents static backfire in drizzle.'
Mercenary: 'Can you turn lead into gold?' Mage: 'I can turn armored knights into slag; sell that instead.'
Mercenary: 'Your robes are singed at the hem.' Mage: 'Acceptable wear during field experimentation.'
Mercenary: 'What's humming in your satchel?' Mage: 'A quartz lens reacting to local stupidity.'
Mercenary: 'Should we drink the blue potion?' Mage: 'Only if you enjoy indigo teeth and mild migraines.'
Mercenary: 'Is that ruin cursed?' Mage: 'Statistically probable. Let me check the ward geometry first.'
Mercenary: 'The air smells like copper.' Mage: 'Step back unless you enjoy lightning.'
Mercenary: 'Can you dry our cloaks?' Mage: 'I'm an arcanist, not a laundry-maid.'
Mercenary: 'What's glowing in the bog?' Mage: 'Marsh-gas. Keep your torches low.'
Mercenary: 'My sword feels cold.' Mage: 'Good. It'll slow their swings.'
Mercenary: 'Their priest is casting!' Mage: 'Watch him choke on his own syllables.'
Mercenary: 'Need a fire tonight.' Mage: 'Gather dry wood first; magic won't burn mud.'
Mercenary: 'Your eyes are glowing.' Mage: 'Means the ley-lines here are foul.'
Mercenary: 'Careful with that fireball!' Mage: 'Stay out of the blast radius and you're fine.'
Mercenary: 'Is that rune safe?' Mage: 'Nothing inscribed in blood is ever safe.'
Mercenary: 'How much mana left?' Mage: 'Enough to fry the front rank. Hold them still.'
Mercenary: 'Strange mist rolling in.' Mage: 'Not natural fog—keep your wards up.'
Mercenary: 'Can you melt that lock?' Mage: 'I'll shatter it; pick the splinters yourself.'
Mercenary: 'Those wards look thick.' Mage: 'Everything cracks if you strike the seam.'
Mercenary: 'My head's throbbing.' Mage: 'Stop staring directly into the rift.'
Mercenary: 'You burned their banners!' Mage: 'They were ugly anyway.'
Mercenary: 'Water's freezing around us.' Mage: 'Let them slip while we advance.'
Mercenary: 'What did that scroll say?' Mage: 'Roughly: run before the sky falls.'
Mercenary: 'Keep the casters off me!' Mage: 'Just keep their pikes off my robes!'
Mercenary: 'That wardstone's humming.' Mage: 'Plug your ears before it ruptures.'
Mercenary: 'Ash is choking my throat.' Mage: 'Breathe through your sleeve and keep marching.'
necromancer: Mercenary: 'That skeleton keeps staring at me.' Necromancer: 'He's checking your boot-size; don't die near him.'
Mercenary: 'Do the dead talk back?' Necromancer: 'Mostly they complain about unpaid wages and damp soil.'
Mercenary: 'Why weigh coins on brass scales?' Necromancer: 'Habit. Every soul has an exact balance.'
Mercenary: 'Will you raise me if I fall?' Necromancer: 'Only if your contract still has hours left on it.'
Mercenary: 'This graveyard gives me chills.' Necromancer: 'Quiet neighbors. Never once started a tavern brawl.'
Mercenary: 'Why carry an awl and ink?' Necromancer: 'Unwitnessed deaths create dreadful paperwork.'
Mercenary: 'Are we the villains here?' Necromancer: 'We are merely probate auditors with sharper tools.'
Mercenary: 'That censer smells like sage and ash.' Necromancer: 'Keeps the marrow-rot out of your bandages.'
Mercenary: 'Can you curse their captain?' Necromancer: 'Already drafted the lien; watch his sword-arm droop.'
Mercenary: 'Where do those spirits go afterward?' Necromancer: 'Back to sleep, once their tally marks clear.'
Mercenary: 'Don't touch my ration pack.' Necromancer: 'Rest easy; the dead have zero appetite for salt pork.'
Mercenary: 'How long have you kept those books?' Necromancer: 'Long enough to know everyone pays eventually.'
Mercenary: 'Why keep that skull?' Necromancer: 'It still answers questions better than you.'
Mercenary: 'Your thralls smell awful.' Necromancer: 'They don't complain about the rations.'
Mercenary: 'That corpse just twitched.' Necromancer: 'Good. Put it in the front rank.'
Mercenary: 'I don't like this graveyard.' Necromancer: 'Think of it as an armory.'
Mercenary: 'They're piling up fast.' Necromancer: 'Leave them whole; I need fresh hands.'
Mercenary: 'Cold wind from nowhere.' Necromancer: 'The dead are gathering. Let them work.'
Mercenary: 'Don't raise my cousin!' Necromancer: 'Relax. His knees were too bad anyway.'
Mercenary: 'What's in that vial?' Necromancer: 'Grave-dust and quiet. Don't drop it.'
Mercenary: 'Those ghouls look hungry.' Necromancer: 'Feed them the raiders.'
Mercenary: 'Why whisper to the mud?' Necromancer: 'Because the mud remembers who drowned here.'
Mercenary: 'One of your skeletons lost an arm.' Necromancer: 'It still has teeth. Send it in.'
Mercenary: 'This bog reeks of rot.' Necromancer: 'Smells like potential to me.'
Mercenary: 'Will you raise me if I fall?' Necromancer: 'Only if you owe me silver.'
Mercenary: 'Look at those pale lights.' Necromancer: 'Lost souls. I'll give them a task.'
Mercenary: 'Keep those bone-things behind me.' Necromancer: 'They're between you and the axes. Be grateful.'
Mercenary: 'That priest called you cursed.' Necromancer: 'He won't be talking much longer.'
Mercenary: 'Too many enemies!' Necromancer: 'Every one of them is a future recruit.'
Mercenary: 'Your hands are freezing.' Necromancer: 'Comes with the trade.'
Mercenary: 'Blow them apart!' Necromancer: 'Step back—corpse-blight splashes.'
Mercenary: 'Even the ashes stir here.' Necromancer: 'Nothing truly rests under the Cinder Crown.'
